setup: # The changesets CLI behind `bun run changeset`.
# The models are gitignored and about 5 GB. Link the source checkout's copies file by file
# (the folders themselves are tracked for their .gitkeep) so a real key or the core's
# install.sh in this worktree does not download them again.

for d in packages/core/upstream/weights packages/core/upstream/vfms/cradio packages/core/upstream/vfms/moge packages/core/upstream/vfms/rvm; do for f in "$PASEO_SOURCE_CHECKOUT_PATH/$d"/*; do if [ -e "$f" ] && [ ! -e "$d/${f##*/}" ]; then ln -s "$f" "$d/"; fi; done; done
teardown: # Everything else is under node_modules/, tmp/, dist/, packages/openfx/build/ and goes with the directory.

ci.command: bun run check:i18n && bun run test && bun run check:changeset

branchName.instructions:
Branch off `main`, the only long-lived branch. Lowercase kebab-case slug of what the change
does, no kind prefix, no ticket numbers, no author prefix (e.g. installer-package,
guard-major-bumps, fix-first-ci-runs).

commitMessage.instructions:
One line, nothing else: no body, no Conventional Commits type prefix, no trailers, no tool
attribution. A short plain-English imperative sentence, capitalised, no trailing period
(e.g. "Add the one-file Linux installer", "Keep download progress out of logs"). Commit often,
one change per commit.

pullRequest.instructions:
Target base branch `main`. Title is a short plain phrase of what ships (e.g. "One-click
installers for Windows and Linux"). Open with a paragraph saying what is now true for the user
or maintainer and why. Then "How to test:" as a numbered list of steps a person can follow,
using this PR's build comment downloads when it changes a package. End with "Tested here:"
naming what ran green (`bun run test`, `bun run check:i18n`, real hosts or the fake core) and
what was not covered. If a package under packages/ changed, the branch must carry a changeset
(`bun run changeset`, English sentence plus an `es-419: ` line; `--empty` when users notice
nothing). User-facing text goes through `t("key")` in both en and es-419. No tool attribution.
